investigation: All three 2560 × 1440 Sky arms exceeded the 120 Hz interval under load. Cloud trace and compose dominate. The fair trace visits many empty samples, while the denser decks accumulate optical depth and terminate rays earlier. The deck trace costs more per counted sample because it lights a larger share of the samples it visits; the sample counter includes empty visits and excludes the nested Sun sampling. The pass still runs one trace per half-resolution texel, and fixed output work and resource inventories are the same across presets. In the recorded pair no named cloud pass grew by 25% against the simultaneous fair arm. For a fresh pair the record lists the changed pass and its fair and deck timings beside both traces’ sample ratios. Shared load varies between arms. Keep the readback counts and per-pass timings for the whole-frame tuning phase.
estimates: CLOUDS DESIGN cost account: weather <0.1 ms, Sun 0.1–0.2 ms, ground <0.05 ms; profiles and resource bytes recorded separately.
